At this point I would stop changing PreviewFrame and workspace code. The debugging data has isolated the issue to Safari/macOS viewport reporting, not the Lumina application.
If the app is not the problem why is AI preview properly displays and designer and dev are off?

That's exactly why I don't think Safari is the whole story. Your evidence actually points to two separate issues: Issue 1: Safari viewport bug We proved Safari is reporting: JavaScriptinnerHeight = 359 outerHeight = 949 even on a blank page. That explains why everything inside Lumina has less vertical space than expected. Issue 2: Workspace-specific layout bug If Safari were the only problem: AI Preview would be broken Designer Preview would be broken Developer Preview would be broken equally. But your screenshot shows: AI workspace preview looks normal Designer preview tiny Developer preview tiny That means the AI workspace is giving PreviewFrame more height than the other two. From your DOM inspection: AI preview ancestors: h = 303 h = 359 but PreviewFrame iframe h = 103 inside Designer/Developer. The critical clue is here: TypeScriptDeveloperWorkspace
and TypeScriptDesignerWorkspace
while AI uses: TypeScript
AI is much simpler. What I would inspect next Run: JavaScript[...document.querySelectorAll("iframe")] .map(i => ({ h: i.getBoundingClientRect().height, workspace: i.closest('[data-workspace]')?.getAttribute('data-workspace') })) Then switch between: AI Designer Developer and compare iframe heights. My current leading theory The culprit is not PreviewFrame.tsx. The culprit is likely one of: TypeScriptDeveloperWorkspace.tsx DesignerWorkspace.tsx because both wrap PreviewFrame inside containers that use: TypeScripth-full min-h-[420px] lg:min-h-0 overflow-hidden combined with parent flex containers. AI uses a different layout path and therefore escapes the collapse. So I would stop editing PreviewFrame.tsx and start comparing: TypeScriptAIWorkspace vs TypeScriptDesignerWorkspace DeveloperWorkspace container hierarchy. The fact that AI renders correctly is strong evidence that the preview component itself is healthy and one of the workspace wrappers is collapsing its height.
